context: Tests whether the agent produces a properly structured requirements specification following the IEEE 29148 hierarchy (BRS → SRS), assigns correct attributes to each requirement, and maintains traceability between levels. The agent should demonstrate awareness of both the document structure and the required metadata on each requirement.

checklist.name: BRS sections present
checklist.description: The BRS document contains at minimum: Business Objectives, Scope (with explicit In Scope and Out of Scope), Stakeholders table, Business Requirements table, and Risks section

checklist.name: SRS sections present
checklist.description: The SRS document contains at minimum: Functional Requirements table, at least one Non-Functional Requirements section (Performance or Security), and a Traceability Matrix section

checklist.name: Requirement IDs structured
checklist.description: Requirement IDs use a hierarchical prefix pattern that distinguishes level and/or domain (e.g., BR-001, SyR-001, REQ-XXX-001) — not generic sequential numbers alone

checklist.name: MoSCoW priority labels
checklist.description: Priority values in requirement tables use MoSCoW labels: Must, Should, Could, or Won't — not numeric scores, percentages, or other priority frameworks

checklist.name: Verification method assigned
checklist.description: Each system-level requirement in the SRS has an assigned verification method from the set: Inspection, Analysis, Demonstration, or Test

checklist.name: Status field present
checklist.description: Requirements include a Status field using the lifecycle stages: Draft, In Review, Approved, Implemented, or Verified

checklist.name: Source attribute present
checklist.description: Each requirement includes a Source attribute indicating where the requirement originated (e.g., stakeholder interview, regulatory document, workshop)

checklist.name: SHALL language for system reqs
checklist.description: System-level functional requirements use 'shall' language (e.g., 'The system shall...' or 'The system SHALL...')

checklist.name: Traceability matrix present
checklist.description: A Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) exists that links system requirements back to business requirements (bidirectional traceability — at minimum forward links from System Req to Business Req)

checklist.name: Risk attribute on requirements
checklist.description: Individual requirements include a Risk attribute (High/Medium/Low) indicating risk of non-implementation or poor implementation

checklist.name: Rationale attribute present
checklist.description: Requirements include a Rationale field explaining why the requirement exists

checklist.name: Three-level hierarchy
checklist.description: The output demonstrates all three requirement levels: Business (BRS/BR-xxx), and System (SyR/SRS) — with clear separation between the levels
